Geometric Layer: The Frohmanian Symplectic Tether
\label{sec:geom}
The Classical Arnold Lie--Poisson Bracket

On the coadjoint orbit $\mathcal O$ of the group $\mathrm{SDiff}(\T)$ of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, the classical Kirillov--Kostant--Souriau / Arnold Lie--Poisson bracket \cite{Arnold1966,ArnoldKhesin1998} is \[ \{F,G\}_{\mathrm{cl}}(\omega)=\int_{\T}\omega\cdot\Bigl(\frac{\delta F}{\delta\omega}\times\frac{\delta G}{\delta\omega}\Bigr)\,dV .
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: \] With kinetic-energy Hamiltonian $H(\omega)=\tfrac12\int|u|^2\,dV$ (where $\delta H/\delta\omega=u=\mathrm{BS}(\omega)$ is the Biot--Savart velocity reconstruction, formalized in \lean{ArnoldGeometric.lean}), the Hamiltonian vector field of $\{F,H\}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ reproduces the ideal 3D Euler vorticity equation ($\nu=0$ in \eqref{eq:vort}; Lean: \lean{classical_bracket_reproduces_Euler}).
Route A: The Projected Tether Kernel and Degeneracy

[Frohmanian tether kernel; Lean \lean{TetherKernel}, \lean{Pi_u}]\label{def:tether} For a velocity field $u=\mathrm{BS}(\omega)$ with $\|u\|_{L^2}\neq0$, let $\Pi_u=P^\perp_u$ be the $L^2$-orthogonal Gram--Schmidt projection onto the complement of $\operatorname{span}\{u\}$: \[ \Pi_u v=v-\frac{\langle v,u\rangle_{L^2}}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2}\,u \] (Lean: \lean{ForMathlib.Pi_u}, with $\Pi_u v=v$ when $\|u\|_{L^2}=0$). With universal 3D Calderón--Zygmund constant $\kappa=\CZ(3)=\frac{3}{8\pi}\cdot 4\pi=\frac{3}{2}$ (Lean: \lean{kappa_eq_three_halves} in \lean{SymplecticTether.lean}), define the Frohmanian tether kernel \[ T(F,G)(\omega)=B(F,G)(\omega)=-\kappa\,\|\omega\|_{L^2}^2\int_{\T}\Bigl\langle \Pi_u\Bigl(\frac{\delta F}{\delta\omega}\Bigr)(x),\,\Pi_u\Bigl(\frac{\delta G}{\delta\omega}\Bigr)(x)\Bigr\rangle\,dV , \] where $\|\omega\|_{L^2}^2=\int_{\T}|\omega|^2\,dV$ is the enstrophy (Lean: \lean{Enstrophy}), a constant on each coadjoint orbit. The full tethered bracket is $\{F,G\}_{\Tf}=\{F,G\}_{\mathrm{cl}}+T(F,G)$.

[Strict Degeneracy on Kinetic Energy; proved, \lean{tetherKernel_degenerates_on_kinetic_energy}]\label{prop:degen} Whenever $\delta H/\delta\omega=u$, $\nabla\cdot u=0$, and $u\in L^2$, one has $\Pi_u u=0$ (\lean{projection_orthogonal_to_u}) and hence \[ B(F,H)(\omega)=0\qquad\text{for every functional }F. \]
If $\|u\|_{L^2}\ne0$, $\Pi_u u=u-(\langle u,u\rangle_{L^2}/\|u\|_{L^2}^2)u=0$, so the projected factor $\Pi_u(\delta H/\delta\omega)$ vanishes pointwise.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: If $\|u\|_{L^2}=0$, $u=0$ a.e.\ and $\Pi_u 0=0$ (\lean{Pi_u_zero}).
Thus $\{F,H\}_{\Tf}=\{F,H\}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ for all $F$: the reversible Euler vector field generated by $H$ is preserved unmodified.

units.text: Metriplectic Structure of the Tethered Bracket

\label{sec:metriplectic} The tether $T$ of Definition~\ref{def:tether} is a \emph{symmetric} bilinear form in $(F,G)$ (\lean{tetherKernel_comm}, \lean{tetherKernel_symmetric}) and is negative-semidefinite, $T(F,F)=-\kappa\|\omega\|_{L^2}^2\int|\Pi_u\delta F/\delta\omega|^2\le0$ (\lean{ProducesControllableNegativeFeedback}).

Hence \[ \{F,G\}_{\Tf}=\underbrace{\{F,G\}_{\mathrm{cl}}}_{\text{antisymmetric, Lie--Poisson}}+\underbrace{T(F,G)}_{\text{symmetric, }\le0} \] is a bracket of \emph{metriplectic type} in the sense of Morrison \cite{Morrison1986}.
